partners.mechanism_chain: CASP8 (HGNC:1509) —DISRUPTS→ Apoptosis signaling (GO:0006915); Apoptosis signaling (GO:0006915) —LEADS_TO→ Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome type 2B (MONDO:0011804); TP53 (HGNC:11998) —DISRUPTS→ Cell cycle regulation (GO:0007049); Cell cycle regulation (GO:0007049) —LEADS_TO→ Hepatocellular carcinoma (MONDO:0007256); Apoptosis signaling (GO:0006915) —INCREASES→ Cell cycle regulation (GO:0007049). partners.diseaseBName: epidermolysis bullosa simplex with nail dystrophy
partners.mechanism_chain: CASP8 (HGNC:10235) —DISRUPTS→ Fas pathway (GO:0008284); Fas pathway (GO:0008284) —LEADS_TO→ Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (MONDO:0011804); PLEC (HGNC:9033) —DISRUPTS→ Keratin intermediate filament organization (GO:0030669); Keratin intermediate filament organization (GO:0030669) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermolysis bullosa simplex with nail dystrophy (MONDO:0014661); Fas pathway (GO:0008284) —BINDS→ Keratin intermediate filament organization (GO:0030669). Loss-of-function mutations in CASP8 disrupt the Fas pathway, leading to autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome. Separately, loss-of-function mutations in PLEC disrupt keratin intermediate filament organization, causing epidermolysis bullosa simplex with nail dystrophy. Both apoptosis and cell cycle regulation are interconnected processes; impaired apoptosis can indirectly affect cell cycle checkpoints, and disrupted cell cycle control can lead to increased cellular stress and altered apoptotic signaling, thereby converging on a shared molecular and cellular pathology that contributes to both disease phenotypes.
